## Frequently asked questions

What does Optimus do?
Optimus is a leading Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO), delivering
comprehensive, end-to-end solutions from clinical development to commercial manufacturing of Key
Starting Materials(KSMs), Regulatory Starting Materials(RSMs), Advanced Intermediates, Drug
Substances and Drug Products to the global innovative biotech and pharmaceutical companies.
In which areas does Optimus specialise?

Optimus specialises in:
* Exclusive development and manufacturing of Late phase Molecules.
* Custom Manufacturing of KSM’s, RSMs and Advanced Intermediates.
* Backward integration of KSM’s / Intermediates
* Development and Manufacturing of Oral Solids / Semi Solids dosage forms

How does Optimus ensure quality and compliance?
Quality is maintained through stringent standards in R&D and manufacturing, supported by strong
regulatory understanding, IP management, and robust process development, validation, and
tech-transfer capabilities.
What is the scale of manufacturing capacity?
Optimus provides flexible manufacturing capacity from gram-scale to multi-tonne production,
supporting efficient and cost-effective scale-up of complex molecules and niche molecules.
Does Optimus support custom API or formulation development?
Yes. With a team of 150+ scientists and advanced facilities, Optimus offers custom process
development, analytical method validation, tech transfer, and commercial scale-up for both drug
substances and drug products.
What are the advantages of partnering with Optimus?
* 20+ years of industry expertise
* Integrated backward manufacturing offering cost advantage
* High-quality R&D for complex and niche molecules
* Global export capability and regulatory readiness
* Focus on innovation, affordability, and excellence
Can Optimus support technology transfer or process validation?
Yes. Our expertise team has extensive experience in both technology transfer from a third party
manufacturing site as well as process validations under strict quality and regulatory frameworks.
How does Optimus handle regulatory compliance and documentation?
All submissions are supported with complete documentation such as ANDA / DMFs / IMPD , technical
packages, validation reports, and CMC data to facilitate multi-market regulatory filings.
Does Optimus offer finished formulations or only APIs?
Optimus offers both drug substance and drug products developed through its dedicated formulation R&D
and manufacturing units.

##### [ Internal Medicine ][109]

[ View All Internal Medicine ][110]

We’re developing therapies to treat, slow, or prevent disease progression and improve the quality of
life for patients with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular and kidney diseases. 

[Inflammation and Immunology graphical thumbnail portrait image 3]

##### [ Inflammation & Immunology ][111]

[ View All Inflammation & Immunology ][112]

cause of chronic inflammatory diseases at a molecular level

[Vaccine graphical thumbnail portrait image 4]

[ View All Vaccines ][114]

the threat of diseases that were once widespread and oftentimes fatal.

range of regulatory documents. These documents include dossiers (CTD/eCTD), product labels, periodic
safety reports, clinical trial applications, and responses to regulatory queries. In addition, the
regulatory team ensures that the company’s products are registered correctly in each market,
labeling is compliant, and pharmacovigilance systems are in place. Regulatory professionals must
stay up to date with evolving legislation and guidance documents, as non-compliance can result in

management, including post-marketing surveillance, renewals, and variations. Companies often rely on
regulatory intelligence to anticipate changes in global legislation and proactively adjust their
strategies. As global markets expand, pharmaceutical companies increasingly need to harmonize their
regulatory strategies across jurisdictions while addressing country-specific requirements. This need
gives rise to regulatory harmonization initiatives like ICH (International Council for
Harmonisation) and WHO’s collaborative registration procedures.

Ultimately, regulatory affairs ensure that patients have timely access to safe and effective
medications. It helps companies navigate a highly regulated environment, reduce compliance risks,
and bring innovations to market faster. As the regulatory landscape becomes more complex with the
advent of gene therapy, biosimilars, and personalized medicine, the demand for skilled regulatory
professionals continues to rise. For these reasons, pharma regulatory affairs are not just a support
function—they are a strategic pillar of the pharmaceutical business model.

## 2. Key Global Regulatory Authorities and Their Requirements

Pharmaceutical companies operating globally must adhere to regulatory frameworks set by each
country’s competent authority. These agencies oversee the entire lifecycle of pharmaceutical
products—from clinical trials to marketing authorization and post-market surveillance. The major
regulatory bodies include the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency
(EMA), Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in India, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical
Devices Agency (PMDA) in Japan, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia. Each
agency has its own application formats, timelines, electronic submission systems, and regulatory
expectations, making it crucial for regulatory teams to adopt a tailored approach for each region.

The U.S. FDA regulates drugs, biologics, and medical devices through a robust system that includes
pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) meetings, submission of IND applications for clinical trials, and
final approval via NDA (New Drug Application) or BLA (Biologics License Application). The FDA
mandates submission in electronic format via the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) using the eCTD
standard. Additionally, periodic safety reporting, annual updates, and compliance with labeling and
promotional guidelines are essential post-approval obligations.

The EMA functions under the centralized procedure, where a single application leads to marketing
authorization across all EU member states. It also supports decentralized and mutual recognition
procedures (DCP and MRP) for drugs not eligible for centralized review. EMA requires rigorous
compliance with ICH guidelines and regional documentation in Module 1 of the eCTD. Scientific
advice, orphan designation, and accelerated assessment pathways are additional features companies
can leverage to expedite approvals.

In India, CDSCO governs drug approvals under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. All
applications—whether for clinical trial permission or marketing authorization—must be submitted
through the SUGAM portal. CDSCO places a strong emphasis on local clinical trial data, especially
for new chemical entities (NCEs). Regulatory submissions must include complete CTD modules, and
products are subject to labeling regulations and import license requirements for foreign
manufacturers. CDSCO also monitors pharmacovigilance through PvPI (Pharmacovigilance Programme of
India).

Other notable agencies include Health Canada, ANVISA (Brazil), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), and Swissmedic
(Switzerland). Some countries, like those in ASEAN, follow the ACTD (ASEAN Common Technical Dossier)
format. To manage this global diversity, many companies develop a core dossier strategy that adapts
to country-specific variations. Regulatory intelligence tools and agency guidance documents play a
critical role in maintaining compliance. Successful navigation of these agencies not only
accelerates product launches but also minimizes the risk of rejections or regulatory penalties.

## 3. The Drug Approval Process: From Development to Market Authorization

The journey of a pharmaceutical product from the laboratory to the patient’s hands involves a
multi-phase regulatory approval process. This process ensures that only safe, effective, and
high-quality drugs are made available to the public. While the specifics may vary across regulatory
jurisdictions, the fundamental framework remains largely consistent worldwide. It comprises
preclinical research, clinical trials (Phases I–III), regulatory submission, marketing
authorization, and post-market surveillance. Regulatory affairs professionals are involved at every
stage, ensuring that the data generated meet regional regulatory standards and that submissions are
complete and accurate.

The first phase, preclinical research, involves in-vitro and animal studies to establish the safety
profile of the investigational compound. Regulatory agencies require this data to approve an
Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative
documents. Module 2 serves as a bridge between detailed technical data and the reviewers,
summarizing the quality, nonclinical, and clinical information presented in Modules 3–5. Module 3,

Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative
documents. Module 2 serves as a bridge between detailed technical data and the reviewers,
summarizing the quality, nonclinical, and clinical information presented in Modules 3–5. Module 3,

## BFS-Technologie & bottelpack-Abfüllanlagen

Die [**BFS-Technologie**][39] ermöglicht die Herstellung, Befüllung und Versiegelung von
bruchsicheren Polymerbehältern in einem nahtlosen, vollautomatischen aseptischen Prozess bei
gleichzeitig unübertroffener Flexibilität im Behälterdesign.

[**bottelpack-Anlagen**][40] können bis zu 37.500 BFS-Behälter pro Stunde produzieren. Darüber
hinaus sind sie die platzsparendsten [aseptischen Abfüllanlagen][41] auf dem Markt, optimieren
wertvollen Platz im Reinraum und gehören damit zu den effizientesten auf dem Markt.

Ganz gleich, ob Sie die BFS-Technologie ohne großes Investitionsrisiko testen möchten,
Produktionsspitzen abdecken oder Marktchargen vollständig produzieren wollen – unsere
**[Lohnabfüllung][44] **bietet Ihnen modernste Anlagen und ein umfassendes Servicepaket zu äußerst
wettbewerbsfähigen Preisen.

Zudem bietet unser erfahrenes Team umfassende Unterstützung bei der **Entwicklung **und Optimierung

Technologie

## BFS-Technologie & bottelpack-Abfüllanlagen

Die [**BFS-Technologie**][39] ermöglicht die Herstellung, Befüllung und Versiegelung von
bruchsicheren Polymerbehältern in einem nahtlosen, vollautomatischen aseptischen Prozess bei
gleichzeitig unübertroffener Flexibilität im Behälterdesign.

[**bottelpack-Anlagen**][40] können bis zu 37.500 BFS-Behälter pro Stunde produzieren. Darüber
hinaus sind sie die platzsparendsten [aseptischen Abfüllanlagen][41] auf dem Markt, optimieren
wertvollen Platz im Reinraum und gehören damit zu den effizientesten auf dem Markt.

Salvavidas Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd. is committed to being the world’s leading manufacturer and
exporter of finished dosage forms (FDFs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Our main goal
is to improve patient outcomes while establishing industry-defining standards. We strive to produce
necessary drugs that are affordable, easily available, and effective.

## We are offering
## best Services & Products

High-quality pharmaceutical, ayurvedic, and antibiotic medications are available from Salvavidas
Pharmaceutical, a well-known pharmaceutical manufacturer and supplier in India. Customers can choose
from a variety of packaging solutions for their items, and flexible payment alternatives. They
guarantee on-time delivery and keep their prices competitive. Salvavidas Pharmaceutical puts the
needs of its patients first by improving safety, efficacy, convenience, and compliance while
offering reasonably priced goods that benefit both patients and society as a whole.

medicines on schedule and at fair prices. We promise that every product meets the highest caliber
throughout its development, manufacturing, sale, distribution, etc. We are dedicated to establishing
and preserving solid bonds with our clients worldwide. As a result, we are now recognized as a
reliable exporter offering service globally.

Salvavidas Pharma is a well-known Indian pharmaceutical exporter that provides a wide variety of
medications to international markets. The organization, which is based in Surat, Gujarat, is one of
the greatest places to find pharmaceutical items. It provides a wide range of products that are
developed to fulfill the requirements of its customers, such as antimalarials, analgesics, and
antibiotics. Salvavidas Pharma, which has a large worldwide presence, focuses on public health as a
driver for social and economic advancement. It is currently one of the leading pharmaceutical firms
in India.

## [**Taj Pharmaceuticals**][121], is a [generics pharmaceuticals company][122] with product range
## exceeding 4600 compositions under all therapeutic categories

Taj Pharmaceuticals Limited stands at the forefront of healthcare innovation and compassion. Our
commitment to improving lives is unwavering, as evidenced by our extensive range of pharmaceutical
offerings. We proudly supply prescription solutions, life-saving medications, anti-cancer
treatments, veterinary care products, trusted consumer brands, and cutting-edge CNS drugs.

Our focus extends to a wide spectrum of health concerns, including anemia, anxiety disorders, cancer
and oncology, ear infections, heart failure, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, influenza, non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma,
obesity, osteoporosis, Parkinson’s disease, pneumonia, transplantation, and various common ailments.

With our headquarters nestled in the vibrant city of Mumbai, India, Taj Pharmaceuticals India
Business continues to lead the way in providing healthcare solutions that empower individuals and
communities to thrive. Join us on our journey towards a healthier, brighter future.

Taj Pharmaceuticals stands proudly as a global leader in generics, ranking among the top ten
pharmaceutical companies in India. Our legacy in the field of medicine spans over a century, and our
commitment to innovation and excellence shines through. We have taken the forefront in critical
therapeutic areas such as cancer, virology, and transplantation. What sets us apart is the
harmonious fusion of Taj Pharma’s generic and pharmaceutical divisions, backed by cutting-edge
genetic sciences, allowing us to craft personalized healthcare solutions tailored precisely to
individual patient needs.

At Taj Pharmaceuticals, our mission is clear – to alleviate suffering and elevate the quality of
life for people worldwide. We have tirelessly pursued this noble goal with unwavering patience,
dedication, imagination, and expertise. Our vision revolves around the creation of targeted
medicines and diagnostic tools, uniting to provide patients, physicians, and payers with superior,
safer, and more cost-effective healthcare solutions.

Welcome to Taj Pharmaceuticals, where a profound vision transforms into reality. We are more than
just a company; we are pioneers in Innovating Generics Healthcare.

Taj Pharmaceuticals Limited operates with an unshakable commitment to earn the trust of doctors,
patients, and customers every single day. We understand that trust is a precious currency, and we
invest daily in becoming champions for our stakeholders.

Over the past decade, Taj Pharmaceuticals Group has been diligently shaping a new paradigm in
healthcare. Throughout our organization in India, we nurture enduring relationships founded on
mutual confidence. This commitment is evident in our actions – our scientists earn trust through

## Over 29000 people impacting lives across the world

Zydus group is headquartered in Ahmedabad, India, and ranks 4th in the Indian pharmaceutical
industry. The group has manufacturing sites and research facilities spread across five states of
Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim in India and in the US and Brazil.

Zydus’ global business has a strong presence in the regulated markets of the US, Europe (France and
